controlify.gui.preferred_profile.tooltip: The profile index Controlify should try to use the next time the game starts.

controlify.gui.controller_selection.tool: Automatic follows whichever controller last gave input. Selecting a device restricts this profile to that controller and uses keyboard mode while it is disconnected.
controlify.gui.load_vibration_natives.to: If enabled, Controlify will download and load native libraries on launch to enable support for enhanced features such as vibration and gyro. The download process only happens once and only downloads for your specific OS. Disabling this will not delete the natives, it just won't load them.
You must enable vibration support per-controller as well as this setting.
controlify.gui.custom_natives_path.toolt: Specify a custom folder where Controlify will save and load it's native libraries. This is an absolute path and is not relative to .minecraft. If you enter an invalid directory, this will be reset. Leave blank for default.
This is an advanced setting. Don't touch it if you don't know what you're doing!
controlify.gui.reach_around.tooltip: If enabled, you can interact with the block you are standing on in the direction you are looking.
controlify.gui.reach_around.tooltip.pari: This is parity with bedrock edition where you can also do this.
controlify.gui.reach_around.tooltip.warn: WARNING: This is an unfair advantage over other players without Controlify, and you will likely be flagged by many anti-cheats. This should only be used in situations where everyone playing recognises that you have this ability and are okay with it.
controlify.gui.server_controlled: The server you are playing on is controlling this setting.
controlify.gui.ui_sounds.tooltip: If enabled, Controlify will play UI sounds when you interact with the UI, like in legacy console editions of Minecraft.
controlify.gui.allow_server_rumble.toolt: Accepts vibration packets from servers and vibrates your controller. If a server is doing this maliciously you can turn it off here.
controlify.gui.notify_low_battery.toolti: A toast will appear when your wireless controller's battery becomes low. (EXPERIMENTAL)
controlify.gui.ingame_button_guide_scale: Scales the in-game controller button guide overlay independently from the rest of the game's GUI.
This value is not 1.0, but this setting is currently broken and will have no effect.
controlify.gui.out_of_focus_input.toolti: If enabled, Controlify will still receive input even if the game window is not focused.
controlify.gui.keyboard_movement.tooltip:
Always emulates keyboard WASD when using analogue inputs like a thumbstick. This also applies to boat handling. Keyboard-like movement is used by default on servers because some anti-cheats do not permit analogue movement.
Enabling this option overrides the analogue movement whitelist and server policies that allow analogue movement.
controlify.gui.analogue_movement_default:
When enabled, analog movement is allowed on every server and the whitelist below is greyed out and ignored entirely. When disabled, only servers on the whitelist get analog movement.
Some server anti-cheats may flag or ban you for using analog movement, so only enable this if you're sure every server you play on tolerates it.
! Disables new server detected toast. Check settings BEFORE joining a new server !
controlify.gui.check_movement_type.toolt: Shows a toast telling you whether analog or keyboard-like movement is active right now.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.title: Dev Functions
controlify.gui.dev_functions.toggle.tool: Show or hide the Dev Functions panel. While hidden, its buttons can't be clicked.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.new_server_: Pops up the toast players see when joining a server that isn't on the analog movement whitelist, exactly as it appears in game. For testing and screenshots.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.marker_floo: How far out the target lock marker keeps shrinking before it holds that size. It shrinks with 1/distance, the same falloff the game gives everything else, so this decides how small it ever gets: four blocks over this number, as a fraction of full size. 67 leaves it about a pixel wide; 24 keeps it a readable diamond at any range. Allowed 8 to 120.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.color_point: How fast the left stick moves the pointer once you have pressed A on a color wheel, in GUI pixels a second. Lower is finer.
controlify.gui.add_server_to_analogue_mo: Whitelist current server for analogue movement
Adds the current server to the analogue movement whitelist.
controlify.gui.analogue_movement_whiteli: Servers listed here will use full analogue movement instead of keyboard-like movement. Only whitelist servers that permit analogue movement, as some server anti-cheats may reject it. A server policy requiring keyboard-like movement takes priority.
controlify.gui.use_enhanced_steam_deck_d: If enabled, Controlify will use an enhanced driver for the Steam Deck to improve compatibility and performance. This is experimental and may have bugs. This driver requires Decky Loader to be installed on your Deck.
controlify.gui.copy_debug_dump.tooltip: Copies a Controlify debug dump to your clipboard. You may be asked to use this if you are seeking support.
controlify.gui.new_options.tooltip: A showcase of the new options in the latest updates.
controlify.gui.new_options.label: This option is new!
controlify.gui.custom_name.tooltip: Name to display for this controller throughout Minecraft.
controlify.gui.horizontal_look_sensitivi: How fast the camera moves horizontally when looking around.
controlify.gui.vertical_look_sensitivity: How fast the camera moves vertically when looking around.
controlify.gui.vmouse_sensitivity.toolti: How fast the virtual mouse moves.
controlify.gui.invert_horizontal_look.to: Inverts the look x-axis. e.g. left becomes right and vice versa.
controlify.gui.invert_vertical_look.tool: Inverts the look y-axis. e.g. up becomes down and vice versa.
controlify.gui.look_input_curve.tooltip: Adjusts how the look input from the joystick is interpreted. A linear curve means the look speed is directly proportional to how far the joystick is pushed. A more exponential curve means small movements of the joystick result in smaller look speeds, and larger movements result in much larger look speeds.
controlify.gui.toggle_sneak.tooltip: How the state of the sneak button behaves.
controlify.gui.toggle_sprint.tooltip: How the state of the sprint button behaves.
controlify.gui.auto_jump.tooltip: If the player should automatically jump when you reach a block.
controlify.gui.no_fly_drifting.tooltip: Disables the slight drifting when you let go of the controls.
controlify.gui.is_lce.tooltip: Makes the controller feeling similar to the Legacy Console Edition. This modifies the maths involved in turning joystick input into look direction.
controlify.gui.show_ingame_guide.tooltip: Show a HUD in-game displaying actions you can do with controller buttons.
controlify.gui.ingame_button_guide_posit: Where the ingame button guide is positioned.
controlify.gui.guide_verbosity.tooltip: How much information is shown in button guides.
controlify.gui.show_screen_guide.tooltip: Show various helpers in GUIs to assist in using controller input.
controlify.gui.ingame_guide_gui_scale.to: Change the GUI scale of the Ingame Button Guide separately from the rest of the game's GUI.
controlify.gui.edit_glyph_positions.tool: Opens an editor to nudge the left and right ingame button guide columns independently, in small pixel increments, so they can be moved away from other HUD elements like beacon effect icons. Requires a connected controller.
controlify.gui.glyph_editor.title: Edit Glyph Positions
controlify.gui.glyph_editor.subtitle: Nudge each side, then press Done to save. The preview is approximate.
controlify.gui.screen_guide_gui_scale.to: Change the GUI scale of the Screen Button Guide separately from the rest of the game's GUI.
controlify.gui.show_keyboard.tooltip: Shows an on-screen keyboard when required. A pop-up keyboard will appear when you focus on a text box, and a static keyboard will appear in the chat screen.
controlify.gui.chat_screen_offset.toolti:
How far up the system on-screen keyboard is. This shifts up the chat box so you can see the chat whilst typing.
This is extremely useful on the steamdeck.
controlify.gui.controller_theme.tooltip: The theme to use for rendering controller buttons.
controlify.gui.axis_deadzone.tooltip: How far '%s' axis needs to be pushed before registering input.
controlify.gui.stickdrift_warning: Warning: Setting this too low will cause stickdrift! This is where the internals of your controller become mis-calibrated and register small amounts of input when there shouldn't be.
controlify.gui.auto_calibration.tooltip: Automatically calibrate the deadzones and gyro of your controller.
controlify.gui.button_activation_thresho: How far a button needs to be pushed before registering as pressed.
controlify.gui.mixed_input.tooltip: If enabled, Controlify will allow you to use both this controller and keyboard/mouse at the same time. This should be used when pairing with Steam Input, where certain advanced controller actions needs to be mapped to these inputs, rather than a gamepad. controlify.gui.controller_mapping.explan: Controller mapping allows you to convert your current controller inputs into something else. You can, for example, emulate a gamepad with a flightstick directly in-game.
controlify.gui.create_gamepad_mapping.to: Create a mapping that emulates a generic gamepad, with ABXY, d-pad, triggers, etc.
controlify.gui.clear_mapping.tooltip: Clears the current mapping for this controller and uses the raw inputs.
controlify.gui.allow_vibrations.tooltip: If the controller should vibrate when you do certain actions.
controlify.gui.allow_vibrations.not_avai: You controller does not support vibration or the vibration natives are not loaded.
controlify.gui.hd_haptics.tooltip: Enables experimental HD haptics support for your DualSense controller.

Adjust how Controlify treats your controller's built in gyroscope.

controlify.gui.group.gyro.no_gyro.toolti: This controller does not support Gyro. You must have a DualSense™ controller or other compatible controller to use this feature.
controlify.gui.group.gyro.no_gyro_steamd: Steam Deck's gyroscope does not currently work with Controlify. For now, use Steam Input to emulate gyro to work as a mouse.
controlify.gui.gyro_look_sensitivity.too:
The percentage of the real-world rotation of your controller to use as look input. For example, rotating your controller 90 degrees, will move the camera 90 degrees, at 100%.
The pitch of your controller is used as up/down and the roll and yaw is used for left/right.
This sensitivity is completely independent of the regular horizontal and vertical sensitivity settings.
controlify.gui.gyro_behaviour.tooltip: How the gyroscope input should be interpreted as look input.
controlify.gui.gyro_behaviour.absolute.t: Absolute: Equivalent to moving the mouse in a direction.
controlify.gui.gyro_behaviour.relative.t: Relative: Equivalent to moving a thumbstick in a direction.
controlify.gui.gyro_yaw_mode.tooltip: Determine how the gyro should move the left/right axis.

controlify.gui.gyro_yaw_mode.tooltip.rol: Use the gyroscope's roll value: tilt the controller side to side.
controlify.gui.gyro_yaw_mode.tooltip.bot: Use both the gyroscope's yaw and roll values. Both rotating the controller left/right and tilting it side to side will move the left/right axis.
controlify.gui.gyro_invert_x.tooltip: Invert the left/right rotation of the gyroscope look direction.
controlify.gui.gyro_invert_y.tooltip: Invert the up/down rotation of the gyroscope look direction.
controlify.gui.gyro_requires_button.tool: How the gyro button behaves. (scroll down to controls).

controlify.controller_submission.message:
Please submit some of your controller info to Controlify's database to get it added in a future update.

Controlify sends the following information:
- Your controller's vendor & product IDs
- Your controller's GUID
- The name of your controller (in the box below)
- The version of Controlify you are currently on

This is completely anonymous and doesn't store any of your personal or account information.

Controlify requires Decky Loader to be installed on your Steam Deck to be able to use the enhanced Steam Deck driver. You can use Controlify without, but you will lose access to: back-buttons, touchpads, gyro, auto game pause, screenshot integration.

controlify.gui.aim_assist.tooltip: Controller aim assist: slows your look input down while the crosshair is near a mob, so you overshoot less. Opens its own screen.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.title: Aim Assist
controlify.gui.aim_assist.tab.general.ex: Aim Assist decides where the aim, snap and swing help on every tab is allowed to run.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.tab.aim_help.e: While a mob is locked, the Lock-On tab's Locked Strength and Locked Range replace Strength and Distance, for each weapon whose Override is on.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.tab.snaps.expl: Snaps go to your locked mob first if it is in Snap Range. Swing Timing Assist's swings can set off Snap on Swing.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.tab.lock_on.ex: While a mob is locked, Locked Strength and Locked Range replace Strength and Distance from the Aim Help tab, for each weapon whose Override is on.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.tab.extras.exp: Drop Range and Flying Drop Range only decide when a lock is let go, never how far aim help reaches.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.mode.tooltip: Where aim assist is allowed to run. Singleplayer & LAN means your own worlds and LAN worlds - one you open to LAN, or one you join from the list of LAN games - but never a server; joining a world by its address counts as a server. It only scales the look input you are already giving, and never moves the camera on its own - except Melee Snap, Ranged Snap and Trajectory Aim, which do exactly that once switched on.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.mode.tooltip.w: Many servers treat any aim assist as an unfair advantage, whatever the implementation. Only use the Everywhere setting on servers you know allow it.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.targets.toolti: Which mobs aim assist will pull towards. Players are only targeted while Target Players is switched on.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.target_players: Other players count as targets too, whatever Target is set to: for the pull, Target Lock and Last hit lock, both snaps, the marker and the compass bar. Spectators, players who are invisible to you, and teammates you cannot hurt because your team has friendly fire off are always left out, and a locked player is let go the moment they stop counting.
WARNING: Aim help against other players is treated as cheating by almost every server and anti-cheat. Players are only ever targeted where the Aim Assist setting allows, Marker only included.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.custom_list.to: Choose which entity types count as targets. Available when Target is set to Custom list.

controlify.gui.custom_list.no_world: Mob previews need a world — the list still works without them

controlify.gui.custom_list.bulk.remove.b: Removes every hostile mob and every passive mob that fights back.
controlify.gui.custom_list.bulk.remove.h: Removes every mob the game classes as hostile, modded ones included.
controlify.gui.custom_list.bulk.remove.p: Removes the passive mobs that fight back: wolf, bee, panda, dolphin, llama, trader llama, polar bear and iron golem.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.melee.tooltip: Used for everything except lining up a projectile shot, including while a crossbow is reloading.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.bow.tooltip: Used while drawing a bow or holding a loaded crossbow. Deliberately gentler and tighter than melee. It only leads a shot or allows for arrow drop with Trajectory Aim switched on.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.strength.toolt: How hard the assist slows your look input and pulls towards a target, as a percentage. 0 does nothing at all; higher slows harder and pulls further each tick.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.cone.tooltip: How far off a mob can be before the assist takes an interest, in degrees. Measured from the edge of the mob rather than its centre, so the crosshair anywhere on it counts as zero.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.distance.toolt: How far away a mob can be and still be helped with, in blocks.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.trajectory_aim: Helps the crosshair onto where a shot from a drawn bow or a loaded crossbow has to go to land on the mob, rather than onto the mob itself: above it, to allow for the drop over the distance, and ahead of it if it is moving. It allows for your own movement too, and aims for the middle of the mob, where a shot has the most room to land. It moves the camera by itself, stick moving or not, as hard as Strength allows, and Crosshair Cone reaches out from anywhere between the mob and that point. Which mobs it aims for is Lock-On Only's choice, below: only the mob locked with Lock Target, or any mob you settle the crosshair on. Lag Compensation below allows for what you see of a mob being behind where the server has it. Every shot still has a little random spread the game adds, which nothing can allow for.
Bow aim assist helps you onto the mob itself, as it always has, and never leads a shot or allows for arrow drop.

Aims for a fully drawn bow the whole time, so the crosshair holds still while you draw. Let go early and the arrow falls short. A loaded crossbow always shoots at the same speed, so it gets the same help either way.

Aims for the bow as drawn right now, so an arrow let go at any moment lands. A weak early draw has to be lobbed high to reach a mob at all, so until that point comes within Live Start Angle of the full-draw point, it aims for a full draw; then the crosshair makes that last move. A loaded crossbow always shoots at the same speed, so it gets the same help either way.

WARNING: Trajectory Aim turns the camera for you, which many servers and anti-cheats treat as cheating. Like the rest of aim assist it only runs where the Aim Assist setting allows, and not at all while Target Lock is set to Marker only.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.trajectory_loc: On, Trajectory Aim aims only for the mob you have locked with Lock Target; any other mob gets the bow's ordinary help onto the mob itself, as with Trajectory Aim off. Off, it also takes a mob the crosshair cone finds, once you have settled the crosshair on it for a moment with the look stick eased off, so panning past mobs with the bow drawn takes none of them; then it keeps that mob for the whole draw, wherever you take the crosshair, while it stays within Distance and in sight. To let it go, push the look stick hard away from it for a moment.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.lag_compensati: What you see of a mob is behind where the server has it, and the server is where a shot flies and lands: behind by your ping, and by the game's own delay in showing you a mob's movement - about 175 ms, there even in singleplayer. A lead worked out from what you see lands behind a moving mob by that much. Lag Compensation takes the mob to keep moving for that long before the shot starts, on top of the flight. It only matters for a mob that is moving, and only with Trajectory Aim on.
No allowance: a mob is taken to be where you see it as the shot starts.
Allows for the Lag Allowance set below. Your ping plus about 175 ms is the place to start; raise it if arrows land behind moving mobs, lower it if they land ahead.

Allows for your ping as the server reports it - the number beside your name in the tab list, which the server updates every 30 seconds - plus about 175 ms for the game's own delay. In singleplayer, where there is no ping, that is the 175 ms alone.
How far behind what you see the server is, in milliseconds, while Lag Compensation is on Manual. A tick is 50 ms.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.live_start_ang: With Trajectory Aim on Live, how close to the full-draw point the point for the draw as it is has to come, in degrees, before the crosshair goes to it. Early in a draw the arrow is slow and has to be lobbed far above the mob to reach it; the crosshair used to swing up there and back down as the draw went on. Lower keeps it steadier for longer and moves it less; at 45 it goes to Live's point as soon as a shot can reach the mob at all.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.swing_timing.t: Hold attack and it keeps swinging for you, each time the weapon in your hand has fully recharged - every 12.5 ticks with a sword - so every swing lands at full strength. The press itself swings as usual and the rhythm counts from there. Holding attack on a block still just mines it.
WARNING: Swinging for you is treated as cheating by many servers and anti-cheats. Like aim assist, it only runs where the Aim Assist setting allows.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.melee_snap.too: Turns the camera onto a mob when you swing at nothing: your locked target if it is within Snap Range, otherwise the hostile mob nearest your crosshair within Snap Angle and Snap Range. Hostile means monsters, and neutral mobs that are angry, whatever Target is set to - and other players while Target Players is on.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.ranged_snap.to: Turns the camera onto a mob as you start drawing a bow, or as a loaded crossbow comes up: your locked target if it is within Snap Range, otherwise the hostile mob nearest your crosshair within Snap Angle and Snap Range. Hostile means monsters, and neutral mobs that are angry, whatever Target is set to - and other players while Target Players is on. With Trajectory Aim on, it turns to where the shot has to go to land on that mob instead.
Snap onto a target when you swing at nothing, swings made by Swing Timing Assist included. A swing at a block or a mob is left alone, so mining and hits are never pulled away, and the swing itself still goes off where you were aiming. Aim assist takes over once the snap lands; push the look stick away from the target to stop one part way.

WARNING: A snap turns the camera for you, which many servers and anti-cheats treat as cheating. Like the rest of aim assist it only runs where the Aim Assist setting allows, and not at all while Target Lock is set to Marker only.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.snap_on_aim.to: Snap onto a target when you start drawing a bow, or when a loaded crossbow comes up. Aim assist takes over once the snap lands; push the look stick away from the target to stop one part way.

WARNING: A snap turns the camera for you, which many servers and anti-cheats treat as cheating. Like the rest of aim assist it only runs where the Aim Assist setting allows, and not at all while Target Lock is set to Marker only.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.snap_range.too: How far away a mob can be for a snap to turn to it, in blocks. A locked target further out than this is passed over for the nearest hostile mob within it.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.snap_angle.too: How far off your crosshair a mob can be for a snap to pick it, in degrees, measured to the nearest edge of the mob. At 180 it reaches all the way round. A locked target is snapped to from any angle.
How fast the camera turns at its fastest during a snap. At 100% that is 600 degrees a second.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.snap_ramp_up.t: How quickly a snap gets up to full speed. At 100% it starts at full speed; lower builds up to it over as much as half a second.
controlify.gui.aim_assist.snap_ramp_down: How quickly a snap slows as it comes in to land on the target. At 100% it stops dead on it; lower eases in over as much as half a second.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.aim_assist_: Reports the mob aim assist is currently tracking, how far off centre it is, and how much your look input is being slowed.
controlify.toast.aim_assist.title: Aim Assist
controlify.toast.aim_assist.inactive: Didn't run. Either the mode is Off, this world isn't allowed, or your last look input wasn't from a controller.
controlify.binding.controlify.lock_targe: Tap to lock on to a target, or move to the next one. Hold to let go. Keybind Mode, on the Aim Assist screen, decides which target a tap picks.
controlify.gui.target_lock.tooltip: Holds one mob as your target instead of aim assist picking whichever is nearest your crosshair each tick. Bind Lock Target under Gameplay in Controller Bindings: tap to lock a mob or move to the next, hold to let go. Keybind Mode decides which mob a tap picks: the nearest, or the one you're aiming at. It never moves your camera on its own.
controlify.gui.target_lock.enabled.toolt: Turns the whole target lock system on. It follows the Aim Assist setting on the General tab, so it won't run anywhere aim assist isn't allowed.
controlify.gui.target_lock.mode.tooltip: How a target comes to be locked.
controlify.gui.target_lock.strength.tool: How hard the assist slows and pulls while a target is locked. Used instead of the melee and bow strengths, each while its Override switch below is on.
controlify.gui.target_lock.range.tooltip: How far away a locked mob can be and still get aim assist, and, in Proximity, how far the bind can reach to lock one in the first place. Melee and the bow each use their own Distance for the aim assist instead while their Override switch below is off. F.O.V Lock has its own reach, F.O.V Range. Drop Range and Flying Drop Range, under Letting Go on the Extras tab, are separate: those only decide when a target you already have is given up.
controlify.gui.target_lock.speed.tooltip: How quickly the assist closes the angle still left to the target. Strength is how hard it pulls; this is how fast it settles onto the mob.
controlify.gui.target_lock.override_mele: While a mob is locked, melee uses Locked Strength, Locked Range and Locked Speed above, and Ignore Crosshair Cone below if it is on, in place of the Melee settings on the Aim Help tab. Switched off, melee keeps its own Strength, Crosshair Cone and Distance for the locked mob - the lock still decides which mob that is.
While a mob is locked, a drawn bow or a loaded crossbow uses Locked Strength, Locked Range and Locked Speed above, and Ignore Crosshair Cone below if it is on, in place of the Bow settings on the Aim Help tab. Switched off, the bow keeps its own Strength, Crosshair Cone and Distance for the locked mob - the lock still decides which mob that is.
controlify.gui.target_lock.override_cone: Normally a locked mob is only helped with while your crosshair is already near it, and the Crosshair Cone setting decides how near. Turn this on and that limit comes off: the assist pulls towards your locked target from any angle, and keeps pulling even when you and the mob are both standing still. It still only reaches as far as Locked Range, and it still only ever moves your aim towards the one mob you locked. Like the Locked settings, it only applies to melee while Override Melee Settings is on, and to the bow while Override Bow Settings is on.

WARNING: This tracks a mob for you rather than helping with aim you are already making, which is an unfair advantage over other players without Controlify, and you will likely be flagged by many anti-cheats. This should only be used in singleplayer, or where everyone playing recognises that you have this ability and is okay with it.
controlify.gui.target_lock.dropout.toolt: How a lock is let go of without holding Lock Target: what a hard push of the look stick away from the mob does, and when a target you have walked away from is dropped. The boundary follows the mob, so it moves as the mob does.
controlify.gui.target_lock.push_away.too: What pushing the look stick hard away from your locked mob does: at least 70% of the way, against the mob - or any way but along with it, while the crosshair is held on it - for a quarter of a second; the same push that lets go of a mob Trajectory Aim is holding. Holding Lock Target and Drop Distant Targets let go as before whichever this is set to. In Marker only there is no aim help to push against, and this does nothing.
controlify.gui.target_lock.push_away.off: Nothing. The lock and its aim help stay on the mob until you hold Lock Target or it is dropped, as before.
controlify.gui.target_lock.push_away.dro: The push drops the lock outright - the marker and the compass go with it, as when you hold Lock Target - and nothing is picked until you ease the stick back. Lock again as usual.
controlify.gui.target_lock.push_away.pau: The push keeps the lock, the marker and the compass, but takes the aim help off the mob so the camera is yours; ease the stick back under halfway and the help is back on it.
controlify.gui.target_lock.auto_drop.too: Off, a lock is only ever let go of when the mob dies or you clear it yourself.
How far you can get from a mob that walks before the drop timer starts. This only ever lets a target go — it has no say in what you can lock, and does nothing at all while Drop Distant Targets is off.
The same, for a mob that flies. They cover ground quickly and are usually further off, so they get more room.
How long you can stay outside the boundary before the lock is let go of.
Nothing is ever locked for you. The bind locks a target, moves to the next one, and lets go when held. Keybind Mode decides which target a tap picks.
controlify.gui.target_lock.mode.marker_o: The bind works exactly the same, but aim assist is switched off entirely. Just the marker and the compass, and no aim help of any kind.
controlify.gui.target_lock.mode.last_hit: The bind still works, and on top of that, hitting a mob in melee or being hit by one takes the lock over.
controlify.gui.target_lock.bind_mode.too: Which mob the Lock Target bind picks. It is the same bind either way, only one Keybind Mode is used at a time, and it applies whatever Mode is set to.
controlify.gui.target_lock.bind_mode.pro: A tap locks the nearest mob within Locked Range, preferring ones on screen, and each tap after that moves to the next nearest.
controlify.gui.target_lock.bind_mode.fov: A tap locks the mob closest to your crosshair, within F.O.V Angle and F.O.V Range. Mobs within F.O.V Priority Range come first: one further out is only picked when none of them are in view. Tap while you are still aiming at the one you have and it moves to the next in that order. A tap with nothing in view keeps what you have.
controlify.gui.target_lock.fov_angle.too: How far off your crosshair a mob can be for F.O.V Lock to pick it, in degrees. Measured to the nearest edge of the mob, the same way as Crosshair Cone, so the crosshair anywhere on it counts as zero.
controlify.gui.target_lock.fov_range.too: How far away F.O.V Lock can pick a mob, in blocks. Separate from Locked Range, which still decides how far away a locked mob gets aim assist: a mob locked further out than that keeps its marker, but gets no aim help until it is within Locked Range, or within the weapon's own Distance for a weapon whose Override switch is off.
How close a mob has to be for F.O.V Lock to put it first, in blocks. Every mob in view within this range comes before any further out, even one nearer your crosshair, so a mob beyond it is only picked when nothing within it is in view. Set to OFF, only the crosshair counts.
controlify.gui.target_lock.reset_percent: How far back inside the boundary you have to come for the drop timer to reset, as a share of the range. Without it, a mob chasing you across the line would restart the count every few steps. A percentage rather than a block count so it stays sensible whatever the ranges are set to.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.target_lock: Reports whether target lock is running, what it is currently holding, how far away that is, and how long until it lets go.
controlify.toast.target_lock.title: Target Lock
controlify.gui.target_lock.marker_compas: How a locked mob is shown to you: a marker over its head, and a compass bar along the top of the screen.
controlify.gui.target_lock.arrow.tooltip: Draws a marker over the head of whatever is locked. Solid when you have line of sight to it, faded when something is in the way.
controlify.gui.target_lock.colors.toolti: Opens one screen with a wheel for each: the marker over a locked mob, and the compass bar along the top. Drag around a wheel for the shade and use the column beside it for brightness.
controlify.gui.target_lock.colors.title: Marker & Compass Colors
controlify.gui.target_lock.compass.toolt: Draws a strip along the top of the screen showing where the locked mob is by bearing, so you can find it again without sweeping the camera around. Off, nothing is drawn.
controlify.gui.target_lock.compass_layou: Opens a screen for moving the compass bar and setting how wide it is drawn, against a live preview of the real thing.
controlify.gui.compass_editor.title: Edit Compass Position
controlify.gui.compass_editor.subtitle: Move it, size it, then press Done to save. The preview is the real bar.
controlify.gui.compass_editor.recentre: Put it back in the middle of the screen
controlify.gui.compass_editor.width.tool: How wide the bar is drawn, end caps included. Wider spreads the same 180 degrees over more pixels, so the marker moves further for the same turn and the bearing reads finer.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.controller_: Reports whether the controller is on a cable or a receiver, and lists every joystick the game can see. It only names the connection once both Learn buttons have been used, because SDL does not report this for every controller. The full list goes to the log either way.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.learn_wired: Press this with the controller connected by cable. One press is enough, whether the game was started wired or wireless. It adds what it can currently see to what it already knows about wired. Nothing is ever forgotten, including by the other button - a path that turns up both ways has to be recorded on both sides, which is what stops it deciding the answer. Press it again in a later wired state if the report comes back unclear.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.learn_wirel: Press this with the controller connected wirelessly. It adds what it can currently see to what it already knows about wireless. Nothing is ever forgotten, including by the other button. Press it again in a later wireless state if the report comes back unclear.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.learn.wait: Not ready yet - wait until this button lights up again. For a few seconds after the controller is plugged in or unplugged, the game can't yet see whether it is on the cable or the receiver, so there is nothing to learn. If it stays greyed out, check the controller is connected.
controlify.toast.connection.none.title: No Controller Attached
controlify.toast.connection.none.descrip: Nothing is connected, so there is nothing to describe.
controlify.toast.connection.not_ready.de: The controller is still finishing connecting, so nothing was recorded. Wait until the Learn buttons light up again, then press it again.
controlify.toast.connection.wired.title: Wired Connection
controlify.toast.connection.unclear.hint: Press the Learn button for whichever way it is connected right now. One of these paths shows up both ways, and recording it on both sides is what stops it deciding the answer.
controlify.toast.connection.unlearned.hi: Press Learn Wired while it is on a cable and Learn Wireless while it is on a receiver. Both are needed before these can be told apart.
controlify.toast.connection.learned.more: Recorded. %s wired and %s wireless path(s) known so far - connect the controller the other way and use the other Learn button.
controlify.toast.connection.learned.comp: Recorded. %s wired and %s wireless path(s) known. Controller Connection will now name them.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.forget_conn: Throws away every path the Learn buttons recorded, for both wired and wireless, so the whole thing can be taught again from nothing. This is the way back from pressing a Learn button in the wrong state, since learning only ever adds. Controller Connection goes back to saying it has not been taught yet.
controlify.toast.connection.forgotten.de: Forgot %s recorded path(s). Use the Learn buttons again to teach it.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.touch_mouse: Makes the mouse stand in for one finger: the left button held is a finger down, moving it while held is the finger moving, letting go lifts it. The mouse goes on working as a mouse too. For trying touch controls without a touchscreen; press again to turn it off. It only moves while the cursor is free - on a screen, not in the world, where the game holds the cursor still.
controlify.gui.dev_functions.touch_show_: Draws every finger the game can see, in the world and over any screen: a dot where it landed, a ring where it is, and at the top left how many are down and how many finger events have arrived. For checking that touch input reaches the mod. Press again to hide it.
